text:
maria: Hey team — customer on POC says live-tail in Console shows log lines but trace IDs are missing, so they can't correlate traces with logs. They can see request ids in our API logs but not in the forwarded ELK index. Anyone seen this pattern?

tyler: Yep. Two common causes: (1) our SDK isn't propagating the header they expect (x-trace-id / x-request-id) or (2) the log forwarder is flattening JSON and dropping nested metadata.

maria: They are using our hosted integration -> ELK via log-drain. They forwarded a sample line: `{"ts":"2026-03-21T10:02:11Z","level":"info","msg":"invoke","meta":{"req_id":"r-123","user":"acct-9"}}` — no trace field.

alex: Ask them to check the request path: are they calling Redwood through a gateway that rewrites headers? If the gateway adds `x-request-id` we need to map that into `trace_id` in the forwarding pipeline.

pranav: Quick troubleshooting steps: 1) enable debug for Redwood live-tail (Console -> Logs -> Live -> toggle DEBUG for 30m), 2) set `LOG_FORWARDER_RAW=true` on the drain config to avoid flattening, 3) verify the forwarder mapping rule `json.trace_id = meta.trace_id || headers.x-request-id`.

maria: How do they set LOG_FORWARDER_RAW on hosted drains?

tyler: We push an override on the customer's drain token. If you give me the drain id I can flip it. Command I run locally: ```
# flips to raw JSON mode
curl -X POST "https://console.redwood-inference.internal/drains/DR-123/override" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"raw":true}'
```

infra-bot: log-drain DR-123: override applied by tyler at 2026-03-21T10:03:01Z (status: pending-restart) :gear:

alex: Also check the forwarder (filebeat/fluentd) mapping — if they use grok it strips JSON keys. Recommend switching to `json` parser. Example mapping: ```
- decode_json_fields:
    fields: ["message"]
    target: ""
    overwrite_keys: true
- rename:
    fields:
      - { from: "x-request-id", to: "trace_id" }
```

pranav: If they have sampling on the log drain, that can drop correlated spans. Ask them to temporarily disable sampling for the POC timeframe.

sara: I can jump into a quick screenshare with them at 10:30 PT to walk the ELK mapping. Want me to set a calendar invite?

maria: Yes please. Also they asked about rate limits — they see 429s when doing long live-tail sessions.

tyler: Live-tail opens a streaming websocket and counts against stream concurrency. For POC we can bump their stream quota temporarily (add +2 streams) or recommend using shorter tail windows. I'll add a +2 override for 24h.

maria: Thanks. Action items: (1) tyler will flip LOG_FORWARDER_RAW on DR-123 and add +2 stream quota for 24h, (2) sara will screenshare with the customer's devops to adjust ELK mappings at 10:30 PT, (3) pranav will confirm whether the gateway preserves `x-request-id` and provide a snippet for the forwarder mapping.

alex: If you need a quick example snippet for matching traces in Kibana, use this KQL: `trace_id : "r-123" OR request_id : "r-123"` once mapping is in place.

maria: Customer will send 10 sample raw log lines to the secure share.

infra-bot: quota-update: streams +2 applied to acct-acme for 24h by tyler at 2026-03-21T10:03:22Z

pranav: One gotcha — some gateways put the header as `X-Request-Id` (capitalization). Our parser is case-sensitive in some configs; normalize with `lowercase_headers: true` in pipeline.

maria: Great, I'll follow up after the screenshare. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

tyler: If the trace still doesn't map after these changes, ask them to paste a raw line here (redact PII) and we'll iterate.

sara: Invite sent to acme-devops + screen share link.

maria: Closing the thread for now — reopening if any unresolved blocks. :white_check_mark:
